Title: Account Executive
Description:
**OVERVIEW**

You are the voice of UnlimitedContent.com (a subsidiary of QuickerLeads) to a book of clients: you run their strategy calls, you own every email they get from us, and you make sure what was promised on the call is what they receive. You are not a project manager. A delivery team executes the work after each call; your job is to decide what gets done, sell the client on why, and hold the relationship through the result.

Most of your day is on the phone. The rest is in your inbox. If you prefer building things to talking to people, this is the wrong role. If you like closing, keeping, and growing accounts and you can write a clear email in under five minutes, keep reading.

**CORE FOCS**

-Logo retention: % of your book still active at month end. Target: ≥ 95% monthly.

-Net revenue retention: (expansion − churn) across your book, in MRR. Target: net positive every month.

-Call cadence: % of active clients who had a strategy call in the last 30 days. Target: 100%.

-Response time: % of client emails answered within one business day. Target: ≥ 95%.

**HOW THE WEEK IS SPENT**

Roughly 40 hours, and about 70% of it is live with clients or writing to them. If the calls-and-inbox share drops below half, something upstream is broken (delivery slipping, scope creep, or too many accounts).

Strategy and check-in calls (50%): 15–25 scheduled client calls per week, 30–45 min each, plus ad-hoc calls when a client asks.

Client inbox (20%): Reading, replying, and approving every outbound client email; two fixed inbox blocks a day.

Call prep and handoff (20%): Reviewing results before each call; writing the post-call brief that the delivery team executes against.

Internal (10%): Daily standup in Slack, weekly book review with the Head of Accounts, flagging at-risk accounts.

**RESPONSIBILITIES, TASK BY TASK**

Strategy calls

Pull the client’s results (rankings, traffic, content shipped, leads) and read the last call’s brief. Cadence: before every call. Done when: 10-minute prep note covering what moved, what didn’t, and the one recommendation for this call.

Run the call: review results, present the recommendation, get a decision on next month’s priorities. Cadence: 15–25× per week. Done when: client has agreed to a specific plan with a deliverable list and dates.

Identify expansion opportunities on the call (more content, added services, a second property) and pitch them. Cadence: every call where it fits. Done when: expansion logged in the CRM with next step and date.

Keep the calendar full: book the next call before ending the current one; chase any client without a call in 21 days. Cadence: daily. Done when: no active client goes 30 days without a call.

Delivery handoff

Write the post-call brief: deliverables, specs, priority order, client-agreed due dates. Cadence: within 2 hours of each call. Done when: brief posted in the client’s Slack channel and project board; delivery lead acknowledges same day.

Review completed work against the brief before it goes to the client. Cadence: as delivered. Done when: work is either approved and sent, or sent back to delivery with specific changes.

Flag any deliverable at risk of missing its agreed date, and reset the client’s expectation before the date passes. Cadence: as soon as known. Done when: client told of the new date before the old one, not after.

Client inbox

Triage all inbound client email twice a day; reply, delegate a fact-find to delivery, or escalate. Cadence: 2 fixed blocks daily. Done when: nothing in the inbox is older than one business day.

Approve or rewrite every outbound email to a client drafted by anyone else on the team. Cadence: daily. Done when: no email reaches a client without your sign-off.

Send the monthly results email: what shipped, what moved, what’s next. Cadence: 1× per client per month. Done when: sent in the first 5 business days of the month.

Retention

Run a save conversation with any client who mentions pausing, cancelling, or cutting scope. Cadence: same day as the signal. Done when: outcome logged (saved, downgraded, or churned) with reason.

Run a 30-day onboarding call for every new client handed over by sales. Cadence: once per new client. Done when: client knows the cadence, the channel, and the first 90-day plan.

Collect a testimonial, review, or referral from happy clients. Cadence: at the 90-day mark and on wins. Done when: logged in the CRM and passed to marketing.

Reporting

Update account status, health, and next call date in the CRM. Cadence: after every call. Done when: CRM reflects reality by end of day.

Weekly book review with the Head of Accounts: at-risk accounts, expansion pipeline, delivery misses. Cadence: weekly. Done when: written list of at-risk accounts with the action and owner for each.

Pass product and delivery feedback from calls to the delivery lead and partners. Cadence: weekly. Done when: themes posted in Slack with examples.

**WHAT THIS ROLE DOES NOT DO**

The role fails when the person drifts into these. Each has an owner already.

* Produce the work. Content, SEO, design, and reporting are built by the delivery team. You brief it, review it, and send it; you don’t make it.
* Project-manage delivery. Task assignment, capacity, and internal deadlines belong to the delivery lead. Your concern is the client-facing date, not who’s doing what.
* Close new business. Sales signs the client and hands them to you at onboarding. Expansion within your book is yours; net-new logos are not.
* Set pricing or discount. You can pitch any offer on the sheet. Anything off the sheet goes to the Head of Accounts.
* Draft every email yourself. Delivery drafts status updates and fact-finds; you approve and send. Final say doesn’t mean sole author.

**WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH**

You report to the Head of Accounts, who owns net revenue retention across all books and sets your targets. Day to day you work in Slack, one channel per client, with the people below.

Head of Accounts. You get: targets, pricing exceptions, escalations, weekly review. They get: book health, at-risk list, expansion pipeline.

Delivery lead. You get: capacity, delivery dates, completed work. They get: post-call briefs, review feedback, client priority changes.

Head of sales. You get: new clients at signup with the deal notes. They get: referrals, expansion intel, feedback on what sold vs. what was expected.

Partners. You get: offer changes, positioning, new sprint products. They get: what clients are asking for that we don’t sell yet.

**WHO THIS IS FOR**

The best fit is a former agency account exec or inside salesperson who got tired of chasing new logos and is good at keeping the ones they have. Someone who has run 20 client calls a week for a sustained period and can prove it.

Must have

* 3+ years in a client-facing role at a marketing, SEO, or content agency, or 3+ years in B2B account management or inside sales with a retention number
* Has carried a book of 25+ accounts and can state their retention or NRR from memory
* Can explain SEO and content marketing results to a non-marketer without notes: what rankings mean, why traffic lags content, what a lead-to-close rate tells you
* Writes a clear, short email fast. We’ll test this.
* Comfortable asking for the upsell on a call and hearing no
* Reliable on a fixed calendar: calls start on time, every time

Nice to have

* Has sold or managed subscription or productized services (anti-retainer models) and can speak to why clients churn from them
* Has used an AI assistant daily for call prep, drafting, or CRM hygiene
* Local-business or home-services client experience

Not a fit

* Wants to do the strategy work hands-on (keyword research, content calendars, audits)
* Needs a manager to set the daily plan
* Treats email as a chore. In this role it’s half the job.

**COMPENSATION AND LOGISTICS**

Independent contractor, full-time hours, remote with Pacific-time call availability. Pay is a monthly base plus a retention-linked variable; the exact figures are an open decision, but the shape should be as below.

Monthly retainer. Basis: fixed. Why: retention work is steady, not spiky. Pure commission pushes people to oversell and under-serve.

Retention variable. Basis: % of retained MRR in the book at month end, paid on cash collected. Why: aligns to the number the Head of Accounts owns; cash-collected basis matches how sales is paid.

Expansion variable. Basis: % of first-month cash on upsells they originate. Why: keeps the sales instinct alive without competing with net-new.

Pay: $50,000.00 - $150,000.00 per year

Work Location: Remote
